title: The Refinance Math Nobody Checks Before Signing
description:
A mortgage refinance can lower your monthly payment and still lose you money if you don't check one number first: the breakeven point. We run the real numbers on a $300,000 loan and show exactly when the closing costs actually pay for themselves.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #mortgage #refinance #personalfinance

segments.text: A mortgage refinance can lower your payment every month and still cost you money - if you don't check one number first.

Three hundred thousand dollars left on the loan. Twenty five years remaining at six point seven five percent. A refinance offer: a new thirty year loan at five point seven five percent, six thousand dollars in closing costs.
The current loan costs two thousand seventy two dollars a month. The refinanced loan: seventeen fifty.
That's three hundred twenty two dollars saved every single month. But the closing costs have to be paid back first.
At three hundred twenty two dollars a month, those savings cross the six thousand dollar closing cost by month nineteen.

slide.headline: Cumulative savings vs. the $6,000 closing cost

segments.text: Stay in the house past month nineteen and the refinance is pure profit. Sell or refinance again before that, and the closing costs never earn their keep.
The lower rate is only half the math.

lines: The rate isn't the whole story.
Breakeven decides if it was worth it.
